added: infra/deployment (@sos-2/infra-deployment): the free-tier deployment foundation as configuration-as-code — a typed environment variable registry for local/preview/production across Vercel/Neon/Upstash/R2/GitHub/execution-body providers (required vs optional per tier, secret vs public classification, documented LOCAL fixture defaults that are credential-free and tier-gated by both registry and loader), fail-closed loadEnvironment (missing REQUIRED variable => typed error naming the variable, never a silent default; shape validation; secret values held in a closure so they are structurally never echoed/logged/serialized — the only serialization path emits [REDACTED])

provider configuration contracts (pure, injectable — loadEnvironment takes a raw record, zero process.env reads in library code): Vercel project scope (apps/web root, nextjs preset, preview/production dimension separation, local tier with no deployment target, 10s request budget vs 60s Hobby hard cap), Neon connection + database/branch naming per tier (sos / sos_preview / sos_local; main / preview/<slug>) with the migration contract (GitHub Actions runner, lexical order, preview-first, every applied run recorded as a deployment revision record), Upstash tier-prefixed namespaces (sos:<tier>:{cache,idempotency,rate-limit,leases,queue}) with bounded TTLs and the NEVER-CANONICAL rule ENCODED as assertNeverCanonical (a namespace declaration claiming canonicity is typed-rejected; canonical: false + positive finite TTL + tier-prefixed naming are all enforced), R2 single-bucket tier prefixes with write-once immutable object rules (overwrite mode, cross-tier keys and missing content anchors are typed-rejected), and the GitHub CI topology contract (thin top-level callers only, frozen verify.yml untouchable, offline verification with names-not-values secret failures)

preview/production isolation as derived resource footprints: every tier's configuration derives its concrete provider resource identities (tier-namespaced by construction), assertFootprintMatchesTier re-derives the exact expected identity set from the same conventions and rejects any foreign identity, assertTierIsolation rejects ANY shared identity between preview and production footprints, and a preview DATABASE_URL pointing at the production database is typed-rejected by comparing ONLY the extracted public database-name segment (credentials never extracted, echoed or compared) — preview NEVER mutates production is enforced before any provider client exists

the secrets policy module: a deterministic secret-shape pattern corpus (GitHub classic/fine-grained tokens, app secrets, Slack tokens, AWS key ids, private key blocks, JWTs, credential-bearing postgres/redis/https URLs, generic SECRET= assignments, provider sk- keys), findings that carry label/line/column/pattern-id but never matched text, redaction to pattern-id markers, names-only required-secret presence validation, and the CI-wired scanner scripts/secret-scan.mjs over the P3-owned files

deployment revision registration: the machine-checkable DeploymentRevisionRecord contract (environment, provider, region from a per-provider region contract, exact 40-hex source revision sha, provider-assigned deployment revision id, RFC3339 registered-at as an injected clock value, rollback pointer) with serialization round-trip validated on both ends, plus the append-only registrar interface and the deterministic InMemoryDeploymentRevisionRegistrar reference implementation (re-registration rejected; rollback pointers must extend the actual chain; first deployment carries null) — the shape later waves wire into System State

provider health diagnostics: the four honest statuses UNKNOWN|UNAVAILABLE|DEGRADED|HEALTHY with a fail-closed aggregate (UNAVAILABLE > DEGRADED > HEALTHY, UNKNOWN sticky, HEALTHY only with at least one probe and every probe HEALTHY), an injectable probe runner (probe functions + injected clock, zero network in library code, offline-testable with fake providers), validateProviderHealth typing a fabricated HEALTHY as a contract violation, and a ProviderHealthTracker whose statuses change only through observed probe reports

execution/body provider configuration structurally isolated from semantic packages: the BodyProviderConfig schema (capability vocabulary mirroring the execution-architecture body advertisement surfaces as an INDEPENDENT typed vocabulary, isolation levels, network policy with the none+open unsafe combination typed-rejected, filesystem scope with host-scope-requires-account-isolation, bounded cost envelopes, task lifecycle requiring create and checkpoints-or-resume, placement with user-device optionality) — ZERO imports from or into packages/*, pinned by tests that scan the module sources (?raw) for forbidden specifiers — providers remain adapters

the long-running work delegation boundary: LONG_RUNNING_DELEGATION_CONTRACT (Vercel request lifetime never owns long-running autonomous work) with the deterministic delegationDecision policy (durable work delegates to external body providers; local-companion work queues until reconnect; request-scoped work within the 10s budget may run inline) and assertDelegationBoundary which type-rejects durable-long-running work targeting the vercel-request runtime, any request-runtime estimate above the request budget or the Hobby hard cap, and delegated work without a body provider reference

docs/deployment/runtime: the runtime operations documentation set (README orientation with the honest NOT_YET_DEPLOYED status, environment matrix, provider roles, preview/production isolation, revision registration flow, provider health runbook, long-running delegation rules, rollback path, secret handling, CI contract verification)
